articleTitle: Stock Market Trends Analysis using Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The stock market is an option for investment and trading. The market volatility and a wide range of other dependent and independent elements that affect the market value of a particular stock make it challenging to anticipate future values. These characteristics make it extremely difficult for any stock market expert to accurately forecast the market's growth and decline. Stock market predictors help determine future stock prices by taking the previous year's data into account. The prediction is done by the various machine learning models. This paper focuses on forecasting future stock values. using various best machine learning algorithms: k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Ada Boost, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost. The performance is analyzed using the MSE. Results show that the XGBOOST model is efficient in generating future stock prices and performs with a mean squared error of 0.004, mean absolute error of 0.014 and R2 score of 0.995.

articleTitle: Optimized Ensemble Machine Learning Model for Chronic Kidney Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The prevalence of chronic kidney illness has been increasing by a rate of 41.5 over the past few years, posing a significant challenge for healthcare systems worldwide. The disease is characterized by a gradual loss of kidney function over time, resulting in the accumulation of waste products and fluids in the body. Early detection and management of CKD are crucial for improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare costs. Machine learning (ML) techniques have been increasingly employed for predicting the risk of CKD and developing effective screening tools. In this study, an ensemble ML model for CKD forecast is projected, which attained an accurateness of 96.5% by utilizing the Kaggle-based chronic kidney disease dataset. The model was constructed using two algorithms, random forest, and bagging, which were trained on a large dataset of CKD patients' clinical and demographic information. The ensemble model demonstrated superior performance compared to each algorithm separately, indicating the efficacy of the ensemble approach in enhancing predictive accuracy. The results of this research indicate that the suggested ensemble model could be a valuable tool for early identification and management of CKD, thus reducing the burden of CKD on individuals and healthcare systems.

articleTitle: SWARAM: Spectral Waveform Analysis using ResNet for Acoustic Music Genre Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Music is a beautiful and enchanting art form that stirs emotions and creates a special connection with our feelings. With the help of streaming services and new releases, over the last decade, there has been a remarkable expansion in the music industry. The increased demand for music has brought attention to how crucial it is to organize music well to improve accessibility and offer more accurate suggestions. Deep learning techniques, which are effective for image classification, are a promising solution for music recognition. However, transfer learning, which uses pre-trained models to improve the performance of new models, has rarely been used for this task. This paper proposes a unique method for categorizing music genres that makes use of transfer learning and ResNet50. MFCCs are used as a representation of the audio data. The GTZAN dataset, a benchmark for music genre recognition, was utilized to assess the proposed method. Techniques for data augmentation have also been studied to increase the capability of the model for generalization. The proposed approach outperforms numerous recently published studies and achieves 94.5 % accuracy.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for Early Detection of Heart Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The prevalence of cardiovascular disease is a significant worldwide health concern. health concern and is responsible for an increased fatality rate. Effective treatment and prevention of heart disease depend on early detection and precise prediction. This work proposes various machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models for the prediction of heart disease based on a large dataset of patient traits and medical indicators defining the presence of heart disease. This work uses various classifiers namely Naive Bayes, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), decision tree, and Logistic Regression for developing an effective heart disease prediction model. These models have been fed with a dataset containing 1025 tuples and 11 attributes such as sex, age, thalach, restecg etc. The proposed model has been developed with a train and test ratio of 80:20, The aforementioned phenomenon has led to the emergence of certain measures, including precision, recall, accuracy, and Fl-measure, as indicators of the achieved results. The results have depicted that out of all the ML and DL models, the Decision Tree exhibited the highest accuracy with a rate of 98.04%. However, MLP has been also identified as the second outperforming model by showing 95.51 % for binary heart disease classification. Furthermore, the performance of Naive Bayes and logistic regression have shown an accuracy of 83.12%, and 84.48%, respectively.

articleTitle: Integration of PLCC modem and Wi-Fi for Campus Street Light Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Street light is one of component of roads and in streets for illuminating during nighttime. Streetlight also plays a significant role in meeting the sustainable development goals of United Nations by 2030. Currently the industry 4.0 enabling technologies has capability to enhance the infrastructure of the streetlight with respect to sustainability. In this study, a wireless system is proposed to real-time monitor and control the streetlight from any location through internet connectivity. The study proposed architecture and also include the circuit diagram of the system in detailed.

articleTitle: Intelligent Music Recommendation System Based on Face Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Music has been considered a form of expression that can treat conditions such as stress, anxiety, and mood swings. The latest research in music psychology shows that music evokes palpable emotions in listeners. People's personality and mood determines what kind of music they prefer to listen to. The areas of the brain that process thoughts and emotions also control tempo, timbre, and music. Although a person's response to music depends on many external factors, we can classify music as kindness, patience, relaxation, and passion, that's why music is a high-quality connector. Industries are also part of us for a long time, backgrounds, languages, hobbies, political leanings and earning degrees, songs, and other streaming apps. Those apps may be used every time and everywhere and they can be used for daily activities, travel, sports, activities, etc. It is an excessive call for as it can be combined with the rapid development of cellular networks and the digital multimedia era, the virtual track has ended up being the main content of many younger human beings. Emotion-based tunes in our device is designed to recognize emotions in actual time and suggest songs primarily based on perceived emotions. This will become an addition to the conventional tune participant apps we had on our telephones before. One of the essential blessings of being concerned in emotional intelligence is purchaser satisfaction. The main motive of this device is to research the user's image, predict the expression of the person and advise songs appropriate to the detected mood.

articleTitle: A Stacked Meta Classifier Approach for Predicting Cardiovascular Diseases
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the world's leading cause of mortality and is a condition that affects the heart and blood arteries. The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that more than 32 % of the global population succumbs to heart disease. An innovative machine learning model for forecasting cardiac disease is presented in this study. On datasets from the University of California, Irvine (UCI), the proposed approach is assessed. The aim of this research is to improvise the effectiveness of integrated individual classifiers and to minimize the chances of misclassification. To achieve this, the authors have developed an ensemble approach known as the Stacked Meta Classifier. Feature selection algorithms are utilized to enhance classification accuracy and decrease the execution time of the classification system by selecting the most relevant features. The selected feature set, determined by feature selection algorithms, is used to assess the classifiers' performance. Performance measuring metrics are employed to evaluate the stacking classifier performance. The stacked classifier is a combination of Naive Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and Decision Tree (DT). The proposed stacked classifier attains an impressive accuracy of 96 percent, surpassing other cutting-edge models by promoting a timely detection of heart disease and can improve survival rates.

articleTitle: Malware Detection in Mobile Devices Using Hard Voting Ensemble Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The steady rise in devices based on the Android operating system has ignited malware developers to invest their energy in launching various attacks targeting these devices. These attacks have caused pandemonium in various spheres of life including data breaches, displaying irritating graphics and loss of money. This has consequently sparked a need to develop techniques that aim at detecting these bad pieces of code in the devices. Lately, various tools that are aimed at detecting these bad pieces of software have been crafted using various machine learning algorithms. This paper reviews some of the work that has been done so far in creating malware detection tools using these algorithms. It then presents a proposed model that is aimed at performing malware detection on these devices using a unique way of incorporating the hard voting ensemble technique, combining Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machine techniques rather than using individual algorithms. This approach, coupled with the latest and very well-balanced dataset comprising 29298 malware files and 29298 benign files resulted in a very efficient model. The technical novelty of our proposed model includes the use of hard voting ensemble classifiers as well as using a large and well-balanced dataset with the latest malware application samples. It was discovered that the hard voting method outclassed all other individual classifiers in terms of accuracy and false positive rates. The model managed to perform malware detection with a satisfying 98.78<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> accuracy as well as a 0.28% false positive rate.

articleTitle: Enhancing Accuracy in Detection of Meningioma Tumour Using RestNet 50 Deep CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Brain tumor diagnosis is critical as the treatment hinges on the location and size of the tumor in the medical field. It is the vital organ in the human body of all living beings as it controls motor skills, decision-making, and all the voluntary or involuntary actions of the body. Brain tumors are extremely fatal as the last stage leads to cancer; however, they can be cured if diagnosed early enough. A meningioma tumor develops via the meninges membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord. Meningioma is one of the uttermost types of deadly tumors and makes up roughly 30% of all cases related to tumors. The death rate is 35% for adults above 40 and 21% for children. MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) is a vital tool for detecting tumors, offering high-resolution insights into brain structures. The paper proposes a ResNet50-based model to detect meningioma tumors from the MRI of the patient. The model is trained using an open-source dataset of images containing the MRIs of patients with meningioma tumors and some images of healthy individuals. The model uses the Adam optimizer and activation function (SoftMax) to optimize results and to normalize the output of the neural network respectively. The model achieved an outstanding accuracy of 96.63% typically greater than other traditional CNN models.

articleTitle: Terraform: Streamlining Infrastructure Deployment and Management Through Infrastructure as Code
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Terraform first appeared in the decade of the 2017 Infrastructure management tools have the potential to revolutionize how we manage IT infrastructure. However, many organizations today report no significant improvements, and some report that using these tools only makes things more complicated. The question of when a person will be able to deploy the infrastructure utilizing the on-go click service arisesas the cloud gives us the click-on-go interface for deploying infrastructure. Using Terraform to deploy the infrastructure with code in a single step is the straightforward answer to the issue. Terraform allows you to write code for numerous resources that will be deployed on your AWS account. Terraform supports a wide range of providers in addition to AWS, including Azure, Digital Ocean, Grafana, etc. Terraform has significantly reduced the time and effort required for deployment, as well as the amount of human interaction required to do it and the associated errors. Before, we had trouble setting up many resources across several cloud providers, but Terraform has made it simple to construct or deploy infrastructure using code, improving our current processand increasing efficiency as we worked on several projects at once.

articleTitle: Automated Mango Type Classification Using CNN-SVM Ensemble: A Deep Learning Approach for Quality Control and Market Analysis in the Mango Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In this paper, a mango-type detection model is proposed that combines feature extraction from a convolutional neural network (CNN) with classification from a support vector machine (SVM). Alphonso, Kent, Ataulfo, Keitt, and Francis are only a few of the five main mango varieties included in the dataset of labelled photos. The CNN automatically recovers complex patterns and distinctive traits from unprocessed images, facilitating efficient feature learning. The SVM classifier then classifies the various mango varieties using these features. Fl-scores ranging from 83.16% to 85.99% in the evaluation results demonstrate great accuracy. The best precision and recall are displayed by Alphonso and Kent, while Ataulfo has the highest Fl score. The Keitt mango variety, however, poses difficulties because recall is comparatively poorer. This CNN-SVM model provides a dependable method for automatically classifying mango types, enhancing quality assurance and market research for the mango sector. To further improve the model's accuracy, future research may look into more sophisticated CNN architectures and transfer learning methods. Overall, this study emphasises how machine learning and deep learning algorithms have the potential to maximise agricultural productivity.

articleTitle: A Novel Heart Disease Prediction System Using XGBoost Classifier Coupled With ADASYN SMOTE
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: According to official data from the World Health Organization, cardiovascular disease stands as the supreme cause of global fatalities. The estimated number is 17.9 million deaths [16] per year. To provide cure proper recognition of illness based on prevailing symptoms is required. Traditional techniques face many problems like delayed or unnecessary treatment to misdiagnosis. This results into increasing health problems of patient and a big financial loss. The situation can be improved by using AI and ML techniques. Over the past few years, substantial endeavors have been dedicated to enhance applications related to computer-aided diagnosis and detection. Previous researches are based on just medical records of patients and not on their day to day lifestyle habits. In this study we have proposed a prediction system using Extreme Gradient Boost (XGBoost) Classifier coupled with ADASYN SMOTE (used to balance the dataset) that can predict the possibility of getting heart disease based on some observations related to lifestyle. The model has achieved the accuracy of 94.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on the dataset Personal Key Indicators of Heart Disease that is based on a recent data collected by Centre Of Disease Control and Prevention (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kamilpytlak/personal-key-indicators-of-heart-disease). The dataset includes the information of around four lakhs people who have shared some basic information related to their health including the fact that they have experienced Coronary Heart Disease (CHD) or Myocardial Infarction (MI). The accuracy of 94.7% has been achieved with XGBoost classifier (highest among six classifiers) on a balanced data which means model will not give biased results and also it is better than previous work [23]. As the dataset is not balanced we have proposed the use of ADASYN SMOTE over SMOTE to balance the dataset.

articleTitle: Review of Artificial Intelligence-Integrated Blockchain for Training Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In the realm of autonomous vehicles, learning is achieved through reinforcement learning. To illustrate, let's consider the task of training a self-driving car to apply the brakes when it approaches a wall. Initially, the car continues to drive until it collides with the wall multiple times. These experiences are then stored in its memory, enabling the car to learn from them. Gradually, through these collisions, the car becomes aware that it must halt when it nears a wall. Traditionally, each car undergoes individual training until it learns to stop automatically and avoid collisions. However, a paradigm shift is proposed in this paper. Instead of isolated learning, each car would be connected to a shared public ledger. This ledger would serve as a platform for cars to exchange their experiences, enabling all vehicles connected to the ledger to learn from a single car's experiences. This collective learning approach eliminates the arduous task of individually training each car. Facilitating this revolutionary concept is the utilization of Blockchain Technology. By leveraging blockchain, cars can collectively enhance their understanding of when to stop, drawing from the valuable experiences shared on the shared ledger. This creates a collaborative ecosystem where knowledge is shared, accelerating the learning process and paving the way for safer and more efficient autonomous vehicles. The integration of Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain Technology in the context of autonomous vehicles holds immense promise. Through the implementation of an artificially intelligent blockchain system, the learning process of self-driving cars can be streamlined, fostering a future where shared knowledge propels advancements in technology and enhances overall safety on the roads. Experience the power of Artificial Intelligence integrated Blockchain, and unlock the full potential of autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Image Analysis of Plant Stress Phenotypes Using Deep Learning and Augmented Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Recent years have seen a significant development in plant stress phenotyping and classification systems based on deep learning, multimodal analysis, and computer vision techniques. To get the most out of machine learning approaches, a plethora of data is required. For the aim of developing models to recognise and diagnose plant stress, it requires a considerable time and effort to gather a sizable amount of training data in the agricultural industry. Data augmentation enriches the variety of training data for machine learning systems without the need to collect new data. Basic image manipulation and deep learning-based image augmentation methods were used to create augmented plant stress disease datasets in this article. The extended simulation shows that the improved dataset made using DCGAN, WacGAN with NST methods performs better than the original dataset produced with traditional picture editing techniques. However, the detection of stress at the time are key variables in determining how much information is available. We'll need to apply data augmentation methods to study performance of different transfer learning techniques. Multi-crop dataset expansion is handled in this study, which is subsequently used to train a bespoke multi-crop stress phenotyping classification.

articleTitle: An Efficient Methodology for Brain Stroke Prediction Using Missing Value Imputation Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Missing values in the medical dataset have a significant impact on accuracy of machine learning models. Imputation of missing data is a crucial task, when it is crucial to use each available data and keep records with missing values. The goal of this paper is to identify an effective imputation technique. This work evaluates performance of several imputation methods to handle missing values. For the study, authors have employed Stroke Prediction dataset from Kaggle. Missing values imputation has been performed using four imputation techniques namely Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE), K Nearest Neighbour (KNN), MEAN, and MODE. The performance of imputation techniques was analyzed with RF (Random Forest) classifier to find out the best imputation method. The findings reveal MEAN imputation technique provides the most promising results among the used imputation methods. The authors of this study have provided a methodology using imputation methods for brain stroke prediction and have thoroughly analyzed the various steps in the process.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Effect of Feature Selection Methods on Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In the present paper, a comparative study for different feature selection methods like correlation, mutual information, Fisher's test etc. has been made. Six datasets have been considered and the three feature selection techniques have been applied to these datasets. Selected features from different datasets using three different feature selection methods have been analyzed and further performance of five different classification algorithms have been examined for these features. Kurskal Wallis test is applied to check whether the performance of these classification algorithms for the selected features using three different feature selection methods for different datasets is the same or not. It is found that in spite of different subsets of features extracted by three different methods, the results of different classification algorithms are identical. The present study provides an important conclusion about feature selection methods that different subsets of features may be equally important and help to extract the most important features.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Multi-Controller in Software Defined Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In a network design, the control plane and the data plane are separated by the architectural concept of software defined networking (SDN). A centralised controller that serves as the only point of control for the whole network is introduced by the SDN architecture. The controller serves as a logically centralized entity in charge of communicating the appropriate rules to a switch's flow table. Using a single controller to handle a lot of flows becomes insufficient. A lot of large-scale networks have employed multi-controller SDN to meet their objectives. In this research, we use a multi-controller infinite buffer waiting queue model to analyze the system performance metrics. Both numerical and simulated assessments are used to illustrate the proposed model.

articleTitle: Empowering Intelligent Manufacturing with the Potential of Edge Computing with NVIDIA's Jetson Nano
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Manufacturing must use technology to meet demand since it is crucial to the supply chain. Particularly, artificial intelligence has been essential in helping to oversee and support the manufacturing process. This study puts forth the notion of how edge computing aids manufacturing. This article uses NVIDIA's Jetson Nano to address the demand for edge computing in preventing resource overstocking and understocking in the production unit. The concept of quality inspection is examined, as well as the quality inspection of the goods received in the production facility and its effective management through the use of image recognition. The paper primarily focuses on the implementation of deep learning and machine learning models on edge devices. By striking a balance between the computational capacity and memory limits, a domain-specific technique is applied for edge computation in the manufacturing industry employing artificial intelligence networks.

articleTitle: A Smart Device Employs Vgg-16 to Identify Brain Stroke Using CT Scan Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Because brain stroke is a potentially fatal medical illness, prompt and correct diagnosis is essential for prompt health treatment, better patient outcomes, and improved mortality. It can take a long time and be susceptible to human error to manually evaluate medical imaging data conventionally for stroke diagnosis. This study examines how Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) can be used to dynamically classify brain strokes in order to overcome these issues. The suggested study employs the VGG-16 CNN model to classify CT scans of the brain following a stroke. For this challenge, the primary extractor is the VGG-16 model, which is initialized using pre-trained weights from the ImageNet dataset. This allows transfer learning to make use of the network's learned features. By using CT scan pictures to diagnose cerebral stroke, the suggested method demonstrates the potential of VGG-16 as a crucial tool for helping radiologists and other medical professionals. The incorporation of these technologies into clinical processes may help to speed up the diagnosis of strokes, allowing for quicker treatments and better patient care.

articleTitle: Modelling of a Non-Linear Dynamic System Using Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) that overcomes typical neural network constraints. Because of its ability to record temporal dependencies and solve nonlinear equations, long-term data can be simply managed. LSTM is intended to alleviate the problems of RNN's vanishing gradient and exploding gradient difficulties. In this paper, we used LSTM to solve nonlinear plant equations with a gradient descent-based back propagation approach and retrieved the plant's output as well as other performance measures including Average Mean Square Error (AMSE) and Total Mean Average Error (TMAE). When the output of an LSTM is compared to that of a feed-forward Neural Network (FFNN), the LSTM outshines the FFNN. All the parameters of both models, such as iteration count and learning rate are kept constant.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Optimization in CNN: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Hyperparameter optimization is an important issue in convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which is an appropriate deep learning network for image classification. Several classical and metaheuristic algorithms are often employed to optimize hyperparameters. In the present paper, different algorithms are compared by using various evaluation measures. The literature reveals that genetic algorithms (GA) and PSO or particle swarm optimization are the most effective algorithms for hyperparameter optimization used in a variety of domains including disease diagnosis; face detection, and handwritten character recognition. Further, it is concluded that optimized CNNs, are essential to the early detection of a variety of diseases, which can assist physicians and clinicians in saving lives by providing accurate and timely predictions.

articleTitle: Comparison of Proposed Plant Leaf Diseases Detection Algorithm with Existing State-Of-the-Art Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Despite a significant increase in population, agriculture still supplies food for everyone. It is crucial to anticipate plant diseases in the agricultural sector at an early stage since doing so will ensure that there is enough food for everyone. Unfortunately, infections can be foreseen at such an early stage in the crop cycle. The paper's objective is to increase farmers' comprehension of cutting-edge methods for decreasing plant leaf disease. Since there are few vegetables other than potatoes, tomatoes, and mangoes, a precise algorithm and machine learning approaches have been designed to identify leaf diseases. This study takes into account samples of mango, tomato, and potato leaves that have anomalies. Based on the suggested algorithm, a comparison study has been conducted with the help of a confusion matrix.

Author Keywords: comparison between proposed algorithm with existing algorithm using confusion matrix

articleTitle: Implementation of Trajectory Control Algorithm in a Dynamic Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Trajectory planning and obstacle negotiation rate are two fundamental problems in mobile robot locomotion. The proposed work addresses the problem of locomotion in mobile robots using Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN). The RBFNN controller initializes if the sensors detected obstacles inside the environment. The proposed RBFNN navigational control algorithm provides smooth and continuous steering angle commands to the robot using sensory reading. Distance received from the sensors for obstacle negotiation and the target-seeking rate is taken as the input parameter of the proposed control algorithm. The output of the control algorithm is the steering angle and optimum trajectory length toward the target. To show the results in terms of simulation, MATLAB and CoppeliaSim GUI platform has been used. To validate the simulation results, a real-time experiment has been proposed in the same environment. The error for path length and navigational time is less than 5% and has been recorded in terms of both environments (simulation and real-time experiment). The simulation and experimental results established the stability check for the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhancing Archeological Building Reconstruction Through Image-Based 3D Modeling and LoFTR
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Archaeological research often relies on the meticulous reconstruction of historical structures and artifacts. However, this process is frequently hindered by the absence of detailed 3D data and the limited availability of well-preserved sites. In response to these challenges, this thesis tries to contribute in rendering the 3D structure of archaeological buildings from 2D unstructured image. In case of damage to the original buildings, its 3D model can be helpful for replication. The images from the internet are taken to train the model using Structure From Motion (SfM) based algorithms. A model named Detector-Free Local Feature Matching with Transformers (LoFTR) is utilized for local image feature matching. Ultimately, the feature points are adjusted to generate a 3D representation of the building. The key stages of structure from motion encompass feature detection and matching, outlier removal, camera pose estimation, point cloud creation, and 3D mesh generation. This reformulation method can reduce the expense and intricacy associated with traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Glaucoma Through the Analysis of Saccadic Eye Movements Employing Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)

authors.preferredName: R V B S Prasanth Kumar

abstract: This study addresses the significant public health concern of glaucoma, a collection of eye conditions resulting in optic nerve damage and progressive vision loss. To conduct our research, we employed a dataset obtained from collaborative efforts between the Amrita School of Engineering in Bangalore and Narayana Nethralaya Hospital during visual field examinations. The dataset, named EXGP, comprises Humphrey Visual Field tests conducted on a sample of 111 patients. Our research investigates the impact of variations in saccadic eye movements on glaucoma performance. This hypothesis is tested through an examination of diverse metrics associated with saccadic eye movements during visual search tasks. The summarizing parameter, Visual Field Index (VFI), is employed. However, for its widespread acceptance, further characterization and comparison with conventional indices used in glaucoma diagnosis, specifically Mean Deviation (MD), are required. Our objective is to define the applicability of VFI in advanced glaucoma cases by contrasting it with MD and the criteria for establishing blindness. Through statistical analysis of confidential eye data, we generated data samples from the provided dataset. Subsequently, a range of machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), K nearest neighbors (Knn), and Logistic Regression (LR), were utilized to predict the presence of glaucoma or normality in individuals. Classification accuracy for the various machine learning models was assessed using appropriate evaluation metrics. Among the three models, Logistic Regression demonstrated the highest accuracy of 0.94 in performing the classification task.

articleTitle: Classification of Rotten Fruits vs Fresh Fruits Using Sequential Model with Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: This research employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to distinguish between ripe and spoiled fruits using deep learning. The CNN model achieves an impressive accuracy rate of 98.79<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in accurately categorizing these two groups. To facilitate model training and evaluation, a comprehensive dataset containing images of both fresh and rotten fruits is utilized. Libraries such as TensorFlow, OpenCV, and matplotlib are employed for efficient dataset processing. The CNN architecture is thoughtfully crafted, incorporating dropout layers to address overfitting and capture intricate fruit image characteristics. A novel approach for categorizing fruit spoilage is introduced, and the study focuses on apples, bananas, and oranges. The model's performance is evaluated using a Kaggle-sourced dataset, yielding an accuracy rate of 98.0% (0.9879), highlighting the effectiveness of the CNN model in discerning between ripe and spoiled fruits. Additionally, the research explores transfer learning techniques for fruit classification.

articleTitle: A Survey on Methodologies and Difficulties in Facial Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Facial Emotion Recognition or Facial Expression Recognition (FER) is a critical area within Pattern Recognition. This paper explores the importance of recognizing facial expressions, traditionally observed through eyes, eyebrows, and mouth movement. Although face-to-face analysis is effective, machine learning (ML), particularly Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based approaches, has achieved success in this field. Despite this progress, several difficulties persist in the recognition process, including occlusion, tilt, illumination, inter-class variance, and more. This study systematically reviews existing methodologies, identifying both a basic structure for recognition and common challenges across various datasets. Additionally, it compares diverse techniques, offering insights into their efficacy in solving frequent difficulties. The paper's findings contribute to the understanding of facial expression recognition and can guide future research in developing more robust and effective solutions.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Prediction of Psychiatric Disorder
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The foundation of the education systems all around the world were shaken up when Covid-19 started spreading its roots worldwide. India of course was no exception to it. While the education sector in India was already undergoing a transformation with the NEP 2020 policy, all the schools and colleges had to be shut down urgently due to the rapid spread of Covid-19. Almost overnight students and teachers had to switch to online learning. At the onset of lockdown around 250 million students were affected due to closure of educational institutes in India. While there was a massive decline in learning outcomes, the physical and mental well-being of the students was also severely impacted. Students lost touch with being socially physical and alternated to being present on social media. However humans are social animals. With deprivation, came a sense of loneliness and that's when physical and mental wellness issues started taking over leading to psychiatric disorders. Our generation are the leaders of the next and ensuring the wellbeing of young minds is a must. Thus there is a need to study and find out just how much Covid-19 is impacting our students and their lives using Artificial Intelligence cum Machine Learning and furthermore act upon it to find solutions to help them. In this paper, we have approached the above problem using the Binary Classification Predictive Model with different logical neural networks.

articleTitle: Driver Drowsiness Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Every day many road accidents are happening across theworld and many people are losing their lives in these accidents. The majority of these incidents are causedby drowsy drivers. Drivers with Sleepiness and exhaustion are the critical issues contributing to road accidents. So, a real-time drowsiness detection model using deep learning algorithms is used to avoid these incidents before they occur. By these algorithms, the sleepiness of the driver is detected by identifying the facial landmarks. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are used in the proposed system to extract essential features from images of faces taken with an onboard camera. A buzzer alarm is activated when drowsiness is detected to alert the driver and remind them to take the appropriate safety precautions. The accuracy of our well-trained model is 95.5% which helps in easy detection of drowsiness.

articleTitle: Copy-Move Forgery Detection Using HOG and LBP Features with Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: A common method of altering images is called “copy-move forgery,” which includes copying and pasting certain areas of a picture to hide or change its information. This work offers a new way to detect copy-move forgery that uses Random Forest machine learning models with LBP and HOG features to handle this kind of manipulation. The image is first processed using grayscale conversion and scaling, after which LBP features and HOG features are retrieved from each image independently. These characteristics record the local texture and gradient details, which are essential for locating replicated regions. These attributes then implemented to train a variety of machine learning models, including k-NN, RF, and SVM. Each trained model individually determines if an image contains a copy-move forgery and is checked for the findings during the detection phase. Additionally, the results from each model's predictions are then combined using a majority vote system. The final forecast for the image is the class label that garners most support. The efficiency of various feature and model combinations has been tested experimentally on a broad dataset. In comparison to previous models, the HOG and LBP features combined with Random forest produce better detection accuracy. The effectiveness of the Random forest in leveraging the advantages of other methods improves copy-move forgery detection as a whole. The suggested technique offers a precise means of identifying digital picture copy-move fraud. It is excellent for a variety of forensic applications where picture integrity is of the highest concern because to its precision, efficiency, and versatility.

articleTitle: A detailed exploration of Document Image Layout Retention techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The main goal of layout retention of document images is to find out the regions of interest in a scanned printed or handwritten document. These sections of interest can be paragraphs, text or non-text portions, headings, tables, etc. The research on layout analysis approaches that have been done over the past few years is summarised in this article. In order to conduct this survey, research articles from Google Scholar, ACM, IEEE, and other sources on various strategies for layout retention have been examined. The majority of the information is taken from reputable journals, and the remaining papers come from various conferences and book chapters. The comparison of several document image layout retention algorithms is discussed in this article. It aids in locating the gaps between several procedures so that an enhanced strategy may be developed to produce better outcomes.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of Different Modulation Schemes for LMLC in 5G Scenario
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In an OFDM, the peak deviation about average is significantly higher. Thus, low PAPR (Peak to Average Power Ratio) fundamentally enhances the cell coverage. At the transmitter side the Power Amplifier must be linear to function properly due to which it does not saturates preventing it from the attenuation. A multicarrier modulation technique is used to transmit the data with the help of sub carriers such as that in case of OFDM (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing). The average area per site is also restricted to a few meters due to the usage of higher frequencies. By using lower frequency that is less than 1GHz it may lead to longer ranges and as large cell arise, fewer base stations are needed to serve a given region making it perfect for the rural regions. LMLC fulfills the requirement of affordable connectivity for rural areas having low mobility. Hence, this paper gives an overview of generating low PAPR using π/2 BPSK modulation scheme with window shaping filter coupled with Reimann Matrix based SLM technique and comparing different modulation schemes for LMLC for 5G scenario.

articleTitle: Predictive Method for Diabetes using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: When the human body lacks sufficient insulin or when body cells become unresponsive to insulin, an excess of glucose remains in the blood. That can lead to serious health problems like renal disease, eyesight loss, and heart disease. Machine learning has the potential to anticipate diabetes. In this paper, the authors have used four classification algorithms: Support vector machine (SVM), K-nearest neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Logistic Regression (LR), to predict diabetes and have conducted experiments using the PIMA Indians Diabetes Dataset (PIDD). SMOTE has been utilized to balance the dataset. Class balancing improved performance of classifiers. After implementing class balancing SVM obtained 78% accuracy, KNN obtained 74% accuracy, RF obtained 85% accuracy, and LR obtained 71 % accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhance Approach on Steganography Using Quantum Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Quantum computing combines computer science with quantum mechanics, and it is a fast-growing research field. The theory of quantum computing has become significant in the secure transmission of keys which can be achieved by implementing quantum mechanics such as polarization. It uses quantum states to permit the classical information and uses quantum entanglement to ensure reliable transmission creating a secure channel. The elementary unit of quantum information is a quantum bit (qubit). These qubits can be transmitted as a two-state system such as spin-half, a two-level atom. The qubits can also be manipulated using polarization techniques. One drawback of quantum computing is side channel attacks which make the information transmitted vulnerable, the attacker can eavesdrop, decline the integrity of the information or the attacker can target the physical implementation of quantum algorithms. Therefore, to prevent side-channel attacks, this paper focuses on developing a novel approach to detect the side-channel attack and rectify the same within a fraction of a second to improve resiliency. The paper initially converts the user-defined key into binary and applies an encryption algorithm to create an image, serving as cover data for the hidden message. After appropriate polarizer selection, the encrypted key is transmitted through a quantum channel. Verification ensures no tampering or eavesdropping, and the image with the hidden message is shared via a classical channel with the intended recipient. Comparative analysis with traditional key security methods, alongside monitoring for third-party eavesdropping using a quantum key simulator, demonstrates the proposed system's over 99% enhancement in secret key security.

articleTitle: Hybrid Classification Model for Network Traffic Density Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Traffic congestion is an increasing challenge in almost all parts of the globe. In the US alone, over $300B is incurred due to overcrowding. Existing work in the field of “Network Traffic Density Estimation” is hampered by a lack of efficient methods for estimating network traffic density, as conventional methods have difficulty keeping up with the ever-changing topologies of today's networks. Optimizing network performance, boosting security, and allowing efficient resource allocation in complex network infrastructures all depend on finding a solution to this problem. The main cause of congestion at the network level is the increase in demand beyond the potential of the transport network. The machine learning techniques is proposed for the traffic density estimation. The machine learning technique is executed in 3 stages, such as to pre-process the data, extract the features and classify the data. This work suggests a hybrid model which is the combination of logistic regression and K-Nearest Neighbors. The proposed method achieved less error rate as compared to other ML techniques. The proposed method achieved 96.55% accuracy, 0.2% execution time and 3.45% error rate. Python is executed to visualize the suggested model with different metrics like accuracy, execution time, are considered to analyze the results.

articleTitle: A Decision Tree Classifier Based Ensemble Approach to Credit Score Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The process of classifying credit scores holds a crucial role in evaluating an individual's creditworthiness, influencing significant financial choices. This study is driven by the dynamic nature of credit scores and the financial sector's need for precise, real-time credit evaluations. This research introduces an ensemble-based method for credit score classification, utilizing a blend of diverse machine learning algorithms to improve accuracy and resilience. The ensemble approach capitalizes on each base classifier's strengths, mitigating biases, reducing overfitting, and enhancing overall classification accuracy. A comparison between the proposed model and existing frameworks demonstrates its competitive edge, surpassing many counterparts with an accuracy of approximately 92.25%. However, the study acknowledges the potential for further enhancement and validation across various datasets. The ensemble-based framework offers a promising avenue to heighten credit score classification accuracy, thereby contributing to informed financial decision-making and reinforcing credit ecosystem stability. Future endeavors involve expanding the model to include more datasets and refining data preprocessing techniques to achieve even more precise predictions.

articleTitle: A Secure Watermarking Based Image Integrity Verification in IoMT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things in healthcare necessitates a secure way to transfer medical images due to the rise of telemedicine. Security breaches in public networks lead to falsification of medical images and further incorrect diagnoses. To address this issue, we propose a multiwatermarking scheme in which logo is embedded in region of interest and text data is concealed in regions of non-interest for providing authentication and integrity verification. Fractal encoding technique is used to ensure the secure transmission of watermarked medical image. Experimental results demonstrate that proposed scheme ensures high visual quality, lossless recovery of text data and high security. The proposed scheme provides better watermarked image quality as compared with state-of-the-art schemes.

articleTitle: Real-Time Weather Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Creation of weather investigation arrangement that would continually and wirelessly examine the weather and observe live surrounding parameters has been discussed. A weather monitoring system can transmit weather information in real time, including parameters and forecasts. It may provide information on parameters like temperature, humidity, air pressure, and altitude ESP32 with a dual-mode Bluetooth system and integrated Wi- Fi has been used. A cloud server is employed to transfer this data in real time to Blynk loT platform. To display data on Blynk and track weather data in real-time, this study uses environmental factors or sensors. Through the comparative analysis of ESP32 with other monitoring devices it has been predicted that results obtained through ESP 32 are more accurate as compared to others.

articleTitle: Efficiency Measurement of k-Partitioning of Mobile WSN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Network partitioning improves the energy efficiency of the network. In this work, the algorithm (KP-MWSN) can determine the no. of partitions (k) required based on the delay tolerance limit of each node of MWSN. It can be fruitful for the events where a small amount of delay can be accepted but efficiency has not been calculated in respect of a metric. So, we have measured the efficiency of KP-MWSN algorithm and the results are compared with the Topology Partitioning Scheme (TPS). The simulation result shows that in every randomly created event the efficiency of KP-MWSN is always better than other related state-of-the-art work.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Application for Classification of Brain Tumors Through MR Images to Detect Malignancy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In the present paper classification of Brain Tumours through MRI imaging as Fine, Medium and Coarse textures is proposed. The other methods of classification of brain tumours that are frequently used are based on size, shape and spread of the tumour. The importance of classifying tumours based on texture is that there is correlation between malignancy of the tumour and the texture of the tumour. The other methods normally don't give this information. In this paper relation between texture of the tumour and it's malignancy has been explored. Four methods of feature extraction have been used, in order to obtain texture information of the tumour. They are, Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM), Gradient Matrix (GM), Laplacian Of Gaussian (LoG) and the Run-Length Matrix (RLM). Once the features are extracted, they are passed to Decision Tree classification algorithm. The classification algorithms classified the extracted features as having Fine, Medium or Coarse textures. The result obtained showed correlation between texture of the tumour and its malignancy. If the texture is predicted as Fine, then it is most likely a non-malignant, or benign tumour, and its diagnosis is most likely going to give a Complete response. A Medium texture would most likely give a Partial response, and is not very malignant. This is important, since knowing this information can benefit the patient and clinicians. This improves the diagnostic confidence of the clinicians and allows them to diagnose and report multiple patients that results in lower cost of the examination as well as access to diagnostics to people living in remote areas.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-based Blockchain Model for the Storage of Maternal Health Records and Safety Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Maternal health refers to all aspects of pregnancy, prenatal and postnatal care. Technological advancements have improved maternal healthcare extensively yet some of the issues that exists in providing healthcare services are data security, informed decisions, reliability and transparency. Use of modern medical technology can help to overcome these issues and lower the number of maternal deaths. In this paper, we have tried to merge blockchain technology with ML enabled predictive analytics algorithm for collecting, analyzing and storing maternal healthcare information protected and predicting the complications degree of risk during pregnancy. As the patient data stored in blockchain cannot be modified, it helps in providing security and reliability. A blockchain based system to predict pregnancy complications has been proposed. To assess this system a dataset has been used that can be accessed publicly.

articleTitle: A Cluster Based Recommendation System for MOOCs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), which give students access to a variety of courses from renowned universities and knowledgeable professors, have completely changed how education is delivered. As there are so many alternatives, it may become difficult for learners to find and choose courses that suit their needs both academically and personally. Uncertainty and bewilderment may result from this overwhelming scene. Finding relevant courses, evaluating the quality of the content, and reviewing how well the courses match with long-term objectives are only some of the challenges. This lack of self-assurance may lead to less-than-ideal experiences, untapped potential, and discontent, which may have an effect on both individual students and educational institutions. By offering learners individualized recommendations based on their preferences and learning profiles, course recommendation systems have become an important tool to address this issue. This research aims to develop a course recommendation system using cluster analysis to group similar courses based on attributes like course ID, title, and description. The system uses a two-step approach: collecting an extensive dataset of MOOCs, preprocessing it, and applying the K-means Clustering algorithm to identify similar groups. This personalized recommendation system can help learners discover relevant MOOCs and meet their individual preferences and goals. The research focused on recommending similar courses using a dataset of 14,952 records. Clustering algorithms and the cosine similarity metric were used to group similar courses together. The model was compared to expert recommendations for each course.

articleTitle: Soft Computing Approach for Early Diabetic Retinopathy Detection with Modified Water Cycle Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The prevention of visual loss in diabetic individuals depends critically on the early identification of diabetic retinopathy (DR). For the purpose of early detection DR, this research proposes a hybrid soft computing technique. The method uses many algorithms to create a classification model that is effective in spotting early indications of DR in retinal images. The aim of this research is to increase the DR classification's precision and dependability, especially for early-stage DR images. With the use of the Multivariate Minimum Redundancy-Maximum Relevance (MRMR) approach, the dimensions of the characteristics are decreased. The modified water cycle algorithm is used to optimize the SVM hyper-parameters for the RBF kernel function. The findings show that the algorithm under consideration has an effective strategy when compared to similar methods in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of DDoS Detection and Mitigation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Distributed denial-of-service or more simply called DDoS attack is one of the most popular existing attack in cyber-security though it is simple to perform it provides very complex background tasks, which makes it a very powerful threat to the cybersec community, denial-of-service is an attack where the at-tacker uses a system to send requests and various packets in or-der to overload the victims system resources and either crash it or make it unavailable to the legitimate user when this is done using various botnets then this is called distributed denial-of-ser-vice in which the botnets carry malware or just send requests at the same time overloading the system. In this paper, we present a comparative study of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) and its prevention, Detection and mitigation techniques. Providing a thorough analysis of existing prevention and detection measures and comparing which among them can provide the best result and suitable for fighting these attacks and testing the accuracy and finding out the feature scores of algorithms used. Including, some points of research with future scope in the field of Distributed denial-of-service and its detection algorithms and preventive techniques.

articleTitle: Analysis of Face Recognition Technique: Plastic Surgery Altered Face
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Human face recognition is used as an efficient tool in criminal identification but it deals with several challenges. One of the challenges that face by the face recognition system is plastic surgery. Plastic surgery is a sub-specialty of general surgery that focuses on correcting, repairing, or recreating defects or abnormalities in the human body, most commonly through the use of surgical techniques. Plastic surgery involves a wide range of subspecialties, such as breast augmentation, body contouring, and reconstructive surgery; however, it may also comprise treatments that are performed on the face. Enhancing face characteristics, fixing flaws, or enhancing attractiveness are the goals of facial plastic surgery. Recently their abrupt change in the field of plastic surgery it become easier to the criminal to pose a new face. In literature several face recognition challenges are addressed but problems in recognition of surgical altered face are not addressed thoroughly. In this paper, I will try to explore all the challenges of plastic surgery on human face recognition systems.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Model for The SmartManufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The efficacy as well as the standards of innovative manufacturing processes can be greatly enhanced by using deep learning models. Creating a hybrid artificial intelligence strategy for recognizing faulty casting products in intelligent manufacturing is the goal of this project. The recommended model uses pre-processed photo attributes to classify defective goods using the swin transform neural network. The objective is to enhance the quality inspection process in smart manufacturing by precisely recognizing and classifying casting faults. Using a matrix of ambiguity, the usefulness of the suggested technique is assessed, demonstrating both its ability to locate damaged products and its potential to improve both production quality and efficiency.

articleTitle: Smart Sight: A Supportive System for Sight Challenged Individuals (SSSCI)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The perceptive skill of vision, which acts as a necessary channel for carrying out everyday chores, is highly critical to humanity's existence. Reduced visual sharpness from diverse causes assumes the character of vision impairment. With a global population of 7.6 billion, studies from several health organizations suggest that seven out of 1000 persons have some degree of blindness. Regrettably, more than 90% of those who are visually impaired live in developing nations. Most people with visual impairments require aids to identify barriers, go about their everyday lives as other people do, and are typically helped by others. Completing their daily tasks is a real-time struggle. So, our goal is to create a SSSCI system with four subsections-Text Detection, Object Detection, Obstacle Detection, and Emergency Locator- that serves as a springboard for individuals to become autonomous in some areas of their lives. A Raspberry Pi and an Arduino have been

articleTitle: 3D-MACNet: A Multiscale Asymetric Convolution Network for Feature Extraction and Classification of Hyperspectral Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning's amazing feature extraction capabilities have led to its widespread adoption in hyperspectral image classification (HSI) applications. However, traditional deep learning methods frequently produce inferior classification results because of the low discriminatory power of the retrieved features. Furthermore, a notable area of interest in research now involves the difficulty of achieving good classification performance in HSIs with a restricted number of samples. This letter offers a unique 3D multiscale asymmetric convolution network (3D-MACNet) for the extraction of features and HSIs classification to address this issue. By adapting the concept of symmetric convolution to the construction of an asymmetric convolution with three identical branches at distinct scales that can retrieve spatial-spectral characteristics from vertical, horizontal, and all perspectives. run on both the new data sets and the freely accessible standard data sets. The provided model has been proven to exceed the other cutting-edge approaches in regard to classification accuracy, according to empirical evidence.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Based Neural Network Framework for Fraudulent Transaction Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In the modern era of interconnected commerce, digital advancements have brought unparalleled convenience to financial transactions. Yet, this progress has also spawned a pressing challenge: the surge in fraudulent activities. From credit card fraud to complex money laundering, these deceptive practices inflict substantial financial losses and erode trust in the financial ecosystem. This paper introduces the Genetic Algorithm-based Neural Network (GANN) framework as a potent solution. GANN merges Genetic Algorithms (GAs) and Neural Networks (NNs), leveraging GA's optimization with NN's pattern recognition GAs emulate evolution to refine solutions iteratively, while NNs mimic brain neural connections to learn intricate patterns. GANN optimizes NN architecture via GAs, adapting to evolving fraud tactics swiftly. At its core, GANN uses GAs to mould NN architecture, evolving structures to capture transactional nuances. Experimentation on a comprehensive dataset shows GANN's prowess, boasting a remarkable 99.25% accuracy in detecting fraudulent transactions. It outperforms existing models, albeit with limitations like relying on one dataset and the potential for architecture optimization. GANN presents an innovative, proactive approach to fraud detection, learning and adapting to evolving fraudulent strategies. Beyond precise detection, it rebuilds trust, crucial for a robust financial ecosystem.

articleTitle: SubCoPLeD: Superpixel Based Color Distribution Driven Plant Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Plant leaf diseases are haveily threatening the agricultural products. It is responsible for losses in agriculture economic. Observing plant leaf for early detection of diseases is essential to control disease spread and reduce its impact on the agriculture economic. Therefore, plant leaf disease automation is required for effectively controlling the plant leaf diseases in agricultural activities. Recent advances in image processing techniques emerged new possibility for plant leaf disease detection in effective manner. This paper present a simple and robust methodology for early and fast plant leaf disease detection using visual of plant leaf. The proposed method utilizes superpixel of the image in several color models jointly with empirically leant thresholds for identification of plant leaf either diseased or non-diseased. This method The experimental results and analysis on publicly available Plant village dataset supports the advantages of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Navigating the Gray Area: A Three-Label Framework for Uncovering Uncertainty in Fake News
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Detecting the veracity of textual content, and distin-guishing between fake and real news, has been greatly improved with the advent of BERT-based transformers. However, an in-herent challenge arises when encountering news articles that fall within the borderline of the latent vector space between fake and real. In this paper, we propose a three-label framework to address this uncertainty issue and leverage an external data enrichment module, Google Fact Check, to handle such cases. Our approach utilizes a constraint dataset for training both the CT-BERT and BERT base models. Experimental results demonstrate that while the BERT base model achieves an accuracy of 80%, the accuracy of CT-BERT, our proposed framework, reaches 93%. This significant improvement in a ccuracy showcases the effectiveness of our approach in tackling uncertainty in fake news detection.

articleTitle: Proposition of a Novel Clustering Methodology for Multi-User MIMO-PD-NOMA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) in association with Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) serves to improve the system's comprehensive performance, specifically in regard to spectral efficiency and reliability, in consort with reducing latency, thereby making it a more propitious candidate for beyond 5G networks. Clustering methodologies have garnered substantial consideration in the domain of wireless communication owing to their capability to improve allocation of resources, efficient management of the network, and comprehensive system performance. NOMA uses Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) technique that tends to get more imperfect with the enhancement in the participating users in the network; therefore, applying clustering aids to be advantageous in such scenarios, wherein users can be assembled into small clusters, with each cluster employing the NOMA principle independently. This paper proposes a novel clustering methodology whose performance is scrutinized in comparison with some of the popular clustering techniques, for a downlink network scenario, in conjunction with MIMO Power-Domain NOMA (MIMO-NOMA), involving Constrained Optimization Power Allocation (COPA) mechanism. The performance of different clustering methodologies is analyzed using a multi-user MIMO-NOMA (MV-MIMO-NOMA) platform, with respect to Sum Capacity, system Bit Error Rate (BER) and varied modulation schemes.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Optimized Feature Network for Polyp Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Polyps are one of the most common problems in human beings where some part on the surface of the body may bulk. This could be cancerous or non-cancerous. However, to segment these polyps it is very difficult to region them properly because of the different anatomy of human body, polyp shape, size etc. The smaller polyps are harder to segment than the bigger ones. Thus, we have proposed a network which helps to segment the polyps despite of its shape and size. The network consists of two major modules. First module is the multi-scale feature fusion. The second module consists of attention module. The purpose of first module is to represent the image clearly as it works upon multiple dilations on different rate. The second module enhances the relevant channel in the feature map by learning weights. The combination of these modules helps in better representation and thus we can further segment it easily.

articleTitle: Customer Segmentation Using K Means Algorithm and RFM Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Customer segmentation and pattern extraction are two of the most crucial features of a business decision support. To expand the business successfully in a cutthroat industry as it is very important to identify the potential of clients as fast as possible. Managers of the organization make wise strategic decisions after identifying the targeted customers and their corresponding purchase patterns. This paper provides an integrated innovative technique for defining target clients and providing to them to increase the organization's revenue. The major objective of this paper is to classify the data of clients into groups on the basis of their characteristics by using the K-means algorithm. RFM model is used to rank and group to customers on the basis of their recent transactions. A new client is assigned to the cluster by taking a mean value as primary indicator. Elbow method is used for selecting the number of clusters initially and Davies-Bouldin score is used to determine optimal number of clusters. Flattened graph and Snake plot for different K values are shown for analyzing the clusters and finalizing the K value.

articleTitle: A Review of Deep Learning based Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In recent years, proliferation of network attacks and cyber threats has underscored the critical need for robust and efficient Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) to safeguard digital assets and sensitive information. Deep Learning (DL) has emerged as a promising technology for enhancing accuracy and effectiveness of IDS due to its ability to automatically extract intricate patterns and anomalies from large-scale network data. This review paper provides a comprehensive survey of DL-based IDS, offering insights into their strengths, limitations, and recent advancements. Due to the necessity of cyber security, numerous researches have been undertaken to categorize the data moving through the network. Intrusion detection is the prominent method of cyber security to identify the intruders and lessen the network hazard. The present study work has concentrated on the necessity and procedure of IDS using DL mechanisms. Reliability and feasibility of IDS depend on performance and accuracy of deep learning. Present research has conducted a review study of conventional research work and focused on the methodology used during IDS detection and classification using ML and DL. The limitation of conventional research work is also presented in problem statement to propose a better deep learning approach in the future.

articleTitle: Detection of Leaf Diseases Based on Ensemble Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The appearance of infections in plantations is the most common cause of crop losses in a variety of crops. Due to lower product quality and a narrower offering of items, these usually result in reduced income for farmers and higher pricing for consumers. Infection symptoms are mostly evident in plant foliage, hence they are widely used to detect and identify diseases. Combined with computational intelligence or soft computing approaches, image-processing tools can help farmers diagnose diseases more effectively. The disease in plants can be identified using traits gleaned from its symptoms. A strategy using an ensemble approach for providing more precise predictions by merging results through different machine learning algorithms. A group of models cooperating to address a shared issue. Ensemble learning uses the strength of a variety of techniques to overcome the particular weaknesses of each model, as opposed to depending just on one model to provide the optimal answer. The set ought to be less error-prone than a single model. Combining many iterations of a projected model is the process of bagging. Before being used, each model is independently trained using an average model. Bagging's objective is to reduce variance below that of any model. In this work, images of leaves comprising healthy class and diseases obtained from the Plant Village dataset are fed into three Convolutional Neural Network architectures namely LeNet, Inception, and VGG16 net achieve an accuracy of 95%, 92%, and 95% respectively and the ensemble model obtains an improvement of 3.5% matched to the standard method.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Network Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The Internet is an extensive and interconnected network of computers and gadgets worldwide. The demand for security measures is more critical as usage and traffic increase. There are both benign and malignant users on the Internet, and they all have equal access to information. Unfortunately, malicious users, also known as hackers, use this access to infiltrate organizations' systems and inflict significant harm. These attacks can take many forms, including stealing sensitive data, disrupting operations, and spreading viruses or malware. Organizations must implement robust security mechanisms to counteract these threats to safeguard their networks, devices, and data. Robust security mechanisms include measures such as firewalls, encryption, antivirus software, and employee training on best practices for online security. By adopting a preventive security strategy, organizations can mitigate the risk of cyber-attacks and protect their critical data. The firewall defends the enterprise from malicious attacks, but no network can be completely secure. So, it is proposed to install IDS on top of the firewall; it monitors any attempt to breach it, gets access to systems on the trusted side, and issues an alert. Using machine learning (ML), an IDS is suggested in this paper. The NSL-KDD dataset is used to test the Logistic Regression (LR), Stacking CV Classifier, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), MLP classifier, Catboost Classifier, Linear Support Vector Machine (LSVM), Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), and XGBoost Classifier technique.
