With a specific focus on algorithmic robustness, we explore a plethora of techniques that enhance the resilience of ML models against adversarial attacks, uncertainties, and potential intrusions within the proposed framework. Furthermore, this paper meticulously examines the responsible application of ML, particularly in sensitive domains, elucidating strategies aimed at aligning technology with societal values and enhancing security. This holistic exploration culminates in the presentation of a comprehensive framework that serves as an indispensable guiding resource for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers deeply committed to harnessing the immense potential of machine learning addressing ethical aspects (22% focus), algorithmic robustness (35% focus), and responsible application (23 %), offering comprehensive guidance.

articleTitle: A Review on Effective Detection and Prevention for DDOS Attack in Cloud Virtual Environment Using Honeypot
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Network communication is increasing day by day in many ways. The cloud is one of the most modern communication environments. This environment gives users easy access to their information whenever and wherever they need it. An organization's electronic information systems can be compromised using a honeypot, which is a deception tool. A honeypot may be used as an advanced security surveillance tool and early-warning system applied properly. Through utilising it, the risks of attacks on networks and IT systems may be reduced. Additionally, honeypots may be used to examine the methods in which attackers attempt to access an information system and to reveal important information about potential security gaps. This study looked at the way existing attack detection and prevention techniques that utilised honeynet performed. The study implemented automated honeypot solutions using virtual machines and centralised system management tools named Puppet. The attacker's source IP address, location, and timestamp were all gathered through a centralized logging systems. However, advances in this technology also open the door to new attacks. In this paper, they performed an extensive examination of distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks and the methods that have been utilized to recognise and stop these attacks. This research will help emerging researchers at this time to grasp research questions and provide optimal solutions to these problems.

articleTitle: Analysing Severity of Breast Cancer using RNA Sequencing Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Breast Cancer is one of the most extensively researched cancers of the human body. This is has led to the creation and development of innumerable methods and techniques to control the growth and symptoms of the cancer way before it could cause any severe damage to other parts of the body. Yet, breast cancer remains one of the most common cancers and also the leading cause of death in women. This has encouraged us to perform our research in this field. While research does exist on the genetic aspect of breast cancer, it is insufficient to derive any conclusive decisions and results from these papers. Fundamentally any research in this domain is limited to either personal data of patients or genetic data exclusively. This paper aims to provide a unique insight by using both personal and genetic data. The researchers use a variety of innovative data wrangling techniques so as to accentuate the strengths of data. Along with this various statistical and machine learning techniques are used to rank the important genes in the dataset. These genes are selected and used to analyze their effect on patients using various machine learning algorithms. This data can be used to aid the healthcare industry in the detection, treatment and prevention of cancer.

articleTitle: Real-Time Plant Leaf Disease Detection using CNN and Solutions to Cure with Android App
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Food is an essential need of human life. So, crop protection is the most important thing, farmers face many problems related to crops and one of the main problems is plant diseases, it is important to recognize what disease is present in the affected crops and how to find treatment. that plants and plant diseases are one of the main threats to food security that must be addressed. However, rapid detection is still difficult due to lack of knowledge. In this digital age, a mobile phone is now within everyone's reach, so this interactive app provides an improved version of a plant disease trained with a CNN to provide real-time information. information about plant diseases and links to treatment so that farmers or end users can easily identify the disease with this plant disease remedy. When users click on a picture of a plant, the disease of the plant and a link to learn how to treat that disease will be displayed. This paper contains the structure of the application created and all the data and results produced by the plant disease detection model and application for the detection and treatment of diseases

articleTitle: Optimization of DG with Enhanced Elephant Herding Optimization in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Conventional and Non-Conventional Centralized power plants far from populations are utilized to generate electric power and this electric power transmits from generating stations to distribution stations over long distance. Distribution systems are generally radial and ring type. The use of radial distribution systems (RDS) is popular because they are straightforward, affordable, and only rely on a single feeder for supply when something goes wrong. Due to the unidirectional flow of electricity in RDS and the large r/x(resistance/reactance) ratio, huge voltage drops, poor Voltage Stability, and significant energy loss occur. Distributed Generation (DG) is installed in the distribution network at the customer's end, but correct installation is necessary to maximize its size and allocation. Meta-heuristic techniques are applied to get solution of the optimize problem of DG site and size. Single as well as Multi-objective problem can be solved using meta-heuristic artificial intelligence techniques such as Enhanced Elephant Herding Optimization (EEHO) by using a load flow technique (Newton Raphson method) for placing small generating units in the distribution system. A Meta heuristic algorithm Elephant herding optimization (EHO) is based on herding behavior of elephants. Enhanced Elephant herding optimization (EEHO) is modified phase of EHO to improve inappropriate divergence towards origin of clan and improve its exploration and extraction aptitude by updating both clan and separating operators.

articleTitle: A Deep Machine Learning Approach for Intrusion Detection in IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: It has proven to be extremely beneficial in various initiatives, including medical automation, defense systems, and even power grids. Essentially, the security surrounding fundamental processing and communications infrastructures is more important compared to the protection of loT networks. However, due to their relatively limited assets and computing capacity, loT devices are vulnerable to a range of attacks. Therefore, defending loT networks from attackers is critical, and this can be achieved through the creation and deployment of effective safety regulations, such as intrusion detection technologies that incorporate specific controllers. In this work, we describe a unique traffic flow classification method for loT networks that employs deep machine learning to identify intrusions. We use a recently released loT database to develop general characteristics using domain values at the protocol packet level. Addressing binary or multi-class categorization, which includes loss of assistance, extended loss of assistance, surveillance, and data theft operations over loT devices, we create a feed-forward neural network framework. Findings from the examination based on the proposed strategy using the prepared information demonstrate a high level of precision in classification.

articleTitle: Managing Metadata in Data Warehouse for Data Quality and Data Stewardship in Telecom Industry - A Compact Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Present telecom industry database provided poor data quality, specifically metadata quality. As a result, decision making data are missing for analyses. Metadata may contain information about the schema of the data so that the data can be transformed into quarriable data objects when required. The data warehouses (DWH) acceptance has grown hugely for data analysis. The main part of data warehouse includes source of data, software for data acquisition, repository, tools for data analysis, and user interface. So many factors are responsible and be critical for DWH successful implementation, they are type of organization, sufficient technical information, project type, work environment, infrastructure, quality of information, quality of system, quality of Service, and quality of relationship. For data quality and its analysis, metadata, and its roles that metadata plays are very important for organization. Metadata management is a central part of the data analysis process. Metadata carries information about data schema that helps to transformed into quarriable data objects when required. For all projects related to data warehouse, the most important factor is metadata. It catches all types of necessary information to design, simplify, build, and use the data warehouse which contains project related data. Functions of metadata system are to collect and store information in single place, which provides an overview for metadata, such as searches, queries, create, maintain, evaluate and managing access of metadata by establishing role-based security. Stewarding metadata is important for the application of data governance practice for enterprise to provide the value and the context for explaining the data and its components to the end users. With the help of the metadata concepts, the organizations can define a business rule for the specific data attribute.

articleTitle: Predicting Parkinson's Disease Risk Through Protein and Peptide Level Analysis: An Evidence from EDA and Machine Learning Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a disabling brain disorder that affects movement, cognition, and mood. Although there is no known cause or cure, it is possible to manage symptoms with treatment. PD affects about 7 million people worldwide and is projected to reach 10 million by 2030. Recent studies have explored protein and peptide levels as potential PD biomarkers that could impact Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) scores. In this research paper, we analyze data from 1,019 patients to predict the UPDRS score based on biomarkers. We leverage Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and machine learning to identify changes in protein and peptide levels that could serve as useful PD risk biomarkers. These analytical techniques utilize protein and peptide levels from general health screenings of patients for early PD detection to uncover patterns and correlations that enable accurate predictive models for UPDRS. This helps in the early detection of PD, allowing effective management and intervention. Our results show that several proteins and peptides are associated with PD risk. These proteins and peptides have a deep impact on the UPDRS score. We also find that the levels of these proteins and peptides are higher in people with PD than in healthy individuals. Finally, we obtain Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) scores from various machine learning algorithms to measure the accuracy of predictions. Analysis with SMAPE reveals the superiority of Random Forest as the best-performing machine learning technique for PD prediction, with a score of 0.37. In conclusion, PD is a complex disorder without a known cure. However, biomarker analysis with machine learning offers promise for early PD detection and gives clinicians and patients hope for early diagnosis and better treatment strategies.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of Multimodal Physiological Signals and Deep Learning for Stress Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Physiological and behavioral information obtained from wearable or mobile sensors has been utilized to estimate self-reported stress levels. However, the reliance on self-reports for stress annotation during studies often leads to a scarcity of labeled data, impeding the development of accurate and broadly applicable stress prediction models. In contrast, sensors can continuously capture signals without requiring annotations. Researchers have endeavored to identify stress using conventional machine learning techniques for analyzing physiological signals. The achieved results, which vary between 50% and 90% accuracy, have produced mixed outcomes. A drawback of traditional machine learning algorithms is their dependency on manually crafted features. Accuracy tends to decline if these features are misidentified. To overcome this limitation, we introduced a deep neural network approach. Deep neural networks eliminate the need for hand-crafted features and instead extract pertinent features directly from raw data through the network's layers. In our study, deep neural networks were employed to analyze physiological data obtained from the DRYAD dataset. The objective encompassed multi class classification for stress detection, where the networks differentiated among low-stressed, medium-stressed, and high-stressed states, effectively distinguishing baseline, stressed, and amused states.

articleTitle: Detecting Fruit Diseases Using Deep Learning and Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The implementation of several agriculture-related issues was made simple by advancements in computer vision technology. The detection of fruit diseases is one such issue. Using deep learning techniques, a lot of study has been done on many fruits, including apples, mangos, kiwis, passion fruit, and others. The most significant contributions made by this field in recent years are outlined in this review paper. In this review, we have performed a technical analysis of deep learning methods for predicting fruit illnesses. Along with the deep learning models utilized, the study also compares various picture acquisition, image pre-processing, and segmentation methods. The study discovered that the most accurate deep learning model can vary based on the system's computing capacity and the data used. In the article directions for future research have also been covered.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Transportation System Using Artificial Intelligence Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) in a variety of fields, particularly in autonomous vehicles and traffic control. It emphasizes the historical backdrop while highlighting AI's aim to mimic human cognitive powers. Discusses the problem of drowsy driving and looks into detecting methods. In-depth discussions of traffic control problems are also covered, along with cutting-edge solutions such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models for detecting pre-drowsiness and inexpensive smartphone technology for road monitoring. These developments demonstrate AI has the power to alter the way that traffic and road safety are managed internationally. In this paper discuss about use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to solve problems in manufacturing, safety, and public transportation in the transportation sector. It talks about AI solutions for sleepiness detection, road monitoring, and autonomous driving. The application of AI promises to revolutionize the industry globally with safer roads, quicker travel, and inventive unmanned technologies.

articleTitle: Advancements in Unsupervised Feature Learning for Image Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: This research addresses the challenge of unsupervised landmark learning in the presence of non-parameter data, where image pairs exhibit significant variations in appearance and posture. Traditionally, unsupervised landmark learning relies on synthetic image pairs with similar appearances but differing postures. However, these synthetic pairs, generated through predefined transformations, do not accurately represent real-world appearance and pose changes. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel approach incorporating Cross-Picture Cycle Compatibility (C3). We iteratively apply the technique of reconstructed exchange twice to establish comprehensive supervision, with a primary focus on maintaining cycle consistency within the framework. Additionally, we introduce a cross-picture flow to ensure the consistency of image landmarks.

articleTitle: Embracing Federated Learning and CNN for Distributed Diagnosis of Lung Diseases: A Novel Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: This study distrubuted learning and machine learning to diagnose lung illnesses, is described in this research report. The experimental design examines four different healthcare customers and six different kinds of lung disorders. The main reason for implementing FL is the pressing necessity to protect patient data privacy. FL is unique because it enables training on decentralized data without explicit sharing. The suggested technique is used to show strong performance in identifying different lung illnesses. To prevent learning from being skewed toward anyone dataset, the local datasets of each client were fed into the model, resulting in a global model with more broad and nuanced learning. For each client and type of condition, the findings were astonishingly constant, with precision, memory, and F1 scores ranging from around 95% to 98% and an unchanging accuracy of 0.99 across all courses and customers. The model was assessed by three distinct averaging techniques-Macro, Weighted, and Micro. Results for the macro-average varied from 89.08% to 91.36%, showing the model's effectiveness across several classes. Results ranged from 90.38% to 91.89%, indicating the model's capacity to adjust to unbalanced datasets using weighted averages. Results ranged from 90.34% to 91.59% for the micro-average, representing the model's global accuracy and recall skills. The robustness of the strategy is shown by the consistently strong performance across a vast clientele and several classifications of lung disorders. This study advances healthcare analytics by showing how sophisticated machine learning models can accurately identify lung ailments while maintaining data privacy. These models are trained via federated learning approaches.

articleTitle: Accurate Classification of Ovarian Cyst Using Topic Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Ovaries are an essential female organ in the reproductive and endocrine system, responsible for healthy development and foster fertility. Occasionally, they are affected by vesicles that are filled with fluid and are referred to as cyst. Most of the ovarian cysts are benign in nature, but in few cases, they can be harmful for the patient and need to be treated at an early phase. Globally, ovarian cyst is a prevalent problem among females. The identification and classification of ovarian cyst is a major task in medical data analysis for healthcare providers. Manual classification of ovarian cyst may lead to delay in the diagnosis of the patient. In this paper, three Topic Modeling algorithms are utilized to classify ultrasound textual reports into cystic and normal ovary reports. The results of the algorithms are analyzed on the basis of six evaluation metrics like, accuracy, precision, recall, etc. Latent Dirichlet Allocation with accuracy of 90.71% is proven to be a better algorithm for ovarian cyst classification compared to Non-negative Matrix Factorization and Latent Semantic Analysis with accuracies of 83.79% and 90.34% respectively.

articleTitle: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles for Crowd Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Detecting the crowd plays a pivotal role as the current population of India has crossed 140 crores and was expected to reach 166 crores by 2050. Detection and analysis of crowds help in ensuring safety, mitigating traffic congestion, preventing accidents etc. The current study explores the effectiveness of the object detection algorithms, namely SSD MobileNetv3 and state-of-the-art YOLO algorithms, in the context of crowd detection. The proposed approach is tested on MSCOCO Dataset and on the custom dataset which were annotated in YOLO format that were collected various parts of the country. Each algorithm was evaluated based on several key performance indicators, including the processing speed, precision, accuracy etc. Furthermore, we investigated various hyperparameters such as input resolution, training epochs to increase the performance of the software. The resulting software was integrated into a Drone, an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) that helps in surveillance for detecting crowd and provide insights related to the crowd prediction in various parts of a city through a dashboard that send alerts to the concerned department to predict and forecast the crowd.

articleTitle: Empowering Biometrics Authentication System Using Decentralized Blockchain Based Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Biometric authentication systems are the most popular way of storing and securing information and has significantly evolved with the passage of time. But the major problem with this system still exists in the world, i.e., weak security which indirectly results in the risk of biometric information leakage which leads to unreliability of its modules, and non-transparency of its information management. On the other hand, Blockchain technology which is a collaborative and unchangeable record-keeping system that simplifies the task of documenting transactions and monitoring resources within a corporate network become popular and drawn major attention of the communities because of its high-end security feature as it is decentralized, its reliability, and durability. This paper highlights the idea of bringing up these two modern technologies together so as to provide more security to biometrics authentication system with the help of blockchain and analyses the challenges with this integration. Also, biometrics will help blockchain to improve its present distributed schemes for digital identity. This will also help in many real-world inventions like smart devices.

articleTitle: Reviewing the Landscape of Deep Learning Approaches for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Rapid and precise identification of breast cancer is crucial in order to improve patient outcomes for this prevalent and life-threatening disease. The emergence of AI and deep learning techniques has opened new avenues for enhancing breast cancer screening and diagnosis. CNNs and ensemble models, among other deep learning architectures, have demonstrated promising results in the analysis of medical pictures and the extraction of useful characteristics for precise diagnosis. Additionally, the use of transfer learning and pretrained CNN models has demonstrated superior performance in classifying breast tumor images. Studies investigating the usage of one-dimensional data conversion into pictures and utilizing stacked ensemble models for increased classification accuracy show that the use of deep learning extends beyond image-based research. These techniques offer potential solutions for addressing the challenges in breast cancer detection, such as distinguishing between benign and malignant tumors and predicting prognosis. By automating the diagnosis process, deep learning algorithms can assist medical professionals in making informed decisions and providing personalized treatment plans. Enhancing the accuracy and reliability of breast cancer prediction models necessitates further research into the incorporation of larger datasets, processing multi-modal data, and advancements in image generation methods. Overall, AI and deep learning hold great promise in revolutionizing breast cancer screening and diagnosis, ultimately leading to improved survival rates and better patient care.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Energy Efficient Internet of Things based Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (loT) has become an important aspect in various domains such as smart cities, healthcare and industrial revolution. There are various concerns of energy consumption ever since the widespread of IOT due to their imitation on the use of resources when it comes to lOT based Wireless sensor Networks, energy efficiency is essential to ensure optimal and cost-effective deployment. This study is a review of energy-efficient lOT based Wireless sensor Networks (WSN), mail focusing on the methods and techniques that can be employed to optimize energy consumption of lOT devices. This study covers various aspects of energy-optimal lOT based WSN including machine leaning approaches and energy efficient communication protocols.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Adaptive Histogram Equalization-Based Image Enhancement Schemes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Most security cameras are designed to capture a wide field view with the aim of covering a large area, and as a result, they often have a lower resolution than other types of cameras. The images in low-light and constricted environments commonly have the drawbacks of non-uniform illumination, low contrast, and large random noise. Many security cameras are intended to operate in low-light conditions, which can also affect the quality of the images they capture. Additionally, the place where the camera is installed, the type of lens and the settings of the camera also affect the quality of the image. Image enhancement of these low-light images is crucial for analysis and investigation for security and safety purposes. In this paper, we study and compare Adaptive Histogram Equalization techniques for image contrast improvement and enhancement for surveillance footage. Conventional Histogram Equalization (HE), along with its improved versions are analyzed and compared. Four image quality assessment metrics are considered; Visual Quality, Absolute Mean Error Brightness (AMBE), NIQUE and BRISQUE.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study Based on Routing Protocols and Data Transmission in M-WSN Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: With the advancements in technology, various kinds of physical actions may now be digitally operated with the click of a button. This has given rise to the concept of IoT to strengthen the MANET-WSN (M-WSN) in a creative perspective. To find the appropriate path, several routing methods transmit control packets and transmitting unwanted network information consume the battery and raise the issue of packet overhead which reduces then network lifespan. Among various issues, high latency, energy consumption, packet drop, network lifetime and insecure data delivery were to name a few. Moreover, a highly reliable, and adaptive routing is lacking that could provide efficient data transmission in mobile node environment. Therefore, in this research, important protocols for routing supported by M-WSN and game theory methodology, with various route discovery algorithms and secure data transmission from source to destination are discussed. This systematic review considers the last 15 years' studies which were found from highly credible sources. This paper presents a comprehensive study of routing algorithms in mobile and static WSN architectures with an emphasis on using game theory as a decision-making tool. The paper begins with a summary of the modern facilities in routing algorithms and then delves into the many game theory-based strategies that have been put forth for this field. The paper concludes with a discussion of the advantages and challenges of using game theory in the context of routing algorithms, and provides recommendations for future research directions. The idea is expanded to include the performance metrics, security measures, and privacy considerations that surround the secure transmission of data packets between different nodes. The comprehensive analysis provides potential solutions proposed by different researchers that can help for future studies aimed at enhancing network information sharing. A number of routing designs were studied from an analytical perspective and their performance with different QoS metrics are discussed.

articleTitle: Advances in Dimensionality Reduction Techniques for Face Recognition: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Face recognition technology has attracted substantial interest owing to its great potential in different applications. However, with the rapid growth in the resolution and dimensions of images represented as matrices, processing them for feature extraction has become difficult. In this paper, we examine various techniques of dimensionality reduction on image data to extract prominent features that will improve the efficiency and accuracy of recognition systems. Additional preprocessing processes were performed on the images in the dataset to improve performance. The initial section of the paper's methodology focuses on implementing several dimensionality algorithms such as PCA, 2DPCA, and 2D(Square) PCA. Subsequently, we explore facial recognition technology such as Eigenfaces. Finally, when the models' performance is evaluated using criteria such as accuracy and training time, an obvious disparity is observed.

articleTitle: Image Classification Using Federated Averaging Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Machine learning privacy and data ownership con-cerns have prompted the exploration of innovative methods to address these issues. This research delves into the realm of image classification using federated averaging algorithms as a promising solution. By capitalizing on federated learning frameworks, multiple collaborating parties can collectively build a machine learning model without the need to share their raw data. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the Federated Averaging algorithm, focusing on its application to image classification tasks. This approach can potentially be used in various applications where data privacy is a concern. The dataset had sixty thousand training photos and ten thousand test images, divided into ten categories. The categories are T-shirt, pant, dress, sweater, coat, sandal, shirt, sneakers, bag, and boots in each example, which was a 28×28 gray-scale image. The study showcases the effectiveness of Federated Averaging in image classification, revealing outcomes that rival those attained through traditional centralized training methods. With a notable achievement of 87.27% accuracy in image classification, this research highlights the practical viability of Federated Learning while upholding stringent data privacy standards.

articleTitle: An Effective Machine Learning Technique for Rice Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Plant diseases, especially those that attack rice leaves, cause serious problems for farmers since they make it more challenging to provide enough food to satisfy the world's growing population. Farmers' livelihoods that rely on agriculture have been threatened by the economic losses brought on by rice illnesses. As a tragic outcome of the hardships they encounter, several farmers have taken their own lives. It is crucial to detect and identify disease-infected plants in order to execute efficient disease management strategies. The Inception V3 model is utilized for disease classification, and the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) autoencoder is employed to reduce noise in images of rice leaves. The dataset is then expanded through data augmentation approaches. The primary objective of the initial stage is to gather photographs of rice leaves from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Once a collection of photographs has been gathered, the images are subjected to processing using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) autoencoder model. This process aims to enhance the quality of the images and eliminate any unwantednoise present in them. Subsequently, data augmentation techniques are employed to increase the volume of the dataset and standardize the dimensions of the images, both of which play a role in training a robust and adaptable model. Diseases are categorized using the popular inception v3 model, which can process vast and diverse picture datasets. This method allows for the precise categorization and detection of a wide variety of rice leaf diseases with the accuracy of 98.8%.

articleTitle: Outperforming Cryptocurrency Price Prediction Using Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Cryptocurrency price prediction is a complex and dynamic task. Cryptocurrencies are highly volatile digital assets impacted by a wide range of variables, including investor mood, legislative changes, market demand, and technical breakthroughs. This research presents a novel approach to cryptocurrency price prediction using Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). The proposed model incorporates proximal policy optimization (PPO) and a Hybrid Convolutional Neural Network Long Short-Term Memory(CNN-LSTM)model. The proposed model was evaluated for three benchmark datasets such as Bitcoin (BTC), Litecoin (LTC), and Ethereum (ETH). This novel approach significantly improves the prediction rate by investigating price movements and optimizing investment returns. The experimental results show the anticipated daily and weekly returns and the actual and forecasted prices using a sentiment analysis approach. The proposed model outperforms existing approaches by obtaining profits scores such as 1.04 for the LTC dataset, 0.98 ETH dataset, and 0.97 BTC dataset. These scores justify the effectiveness of the proposed model by generating favorable returns in cryptocurrency investments.

Author Keywords: CNN-LSTM(Convolutional Neural Network Long Short-Term Memory)

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Approaches for Breast Cancer Prediction Model: Study and Evaluation of Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: Women die worldwide frequency rate from breast cancer also called breast carcinoma is very high in today's era. In this research, machine learning (ML) methods for a breast cancer prediction model are studied and their performances are compared. Breast cancer is a serious and prevalent disease, and early detection of breast carcinoma is critical task that may help health professionals for successful treatment. ML algorithms have been applied to medical imaging data to assist in the early detection of breast cancer. The study analyzes the performance in terms of the accuracy, precision, and Fl-score of four machine learning algorithms (MLA) which include SVC, Naive Bayes, Random Forest and KNN (K-Nearest Neighbor). The study uses a publicly available dataset of breast cancer patients, which includes various clinical and demographic variables. The study provides insights into the performance of Random Forest, Naive Bayes, SVC, and KNN different MLA for detecting breast carcinoma and can assist in the development of more accurate and reliable breast cancer detection models. According to the findings, the SVC performs more accurately than the other algorithms.

articleTitle: Adapting to Technological Disruption: Challenges and Opportunities for Employment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The paper examines the impact of technology on employment and its transformative effects on the modern workforce. Since the 1980s, a phenomenon has been observed in the labour markets of US & European countries which is called Job Polarization. To put it more clearly, the trend known as “job polarization,” is the change in job opportunities from middle-skill jobs to high- and low-skill jobs. As a consequence, middle-skilled workers' share of the labor force has decreased compared with high- and low-skilled workers. Most manual and routine jobs are done by middle-skilled individuals. As an outcome, technologies and robots can readily replace this sector of the labor force. Some jobs shall become obsolete as robots and algorithms become more proficient in performing tasks that humans used to accomplish. Significant changes have taken place in a number of industries, notably manufacturing, logistics, and customer service, which has resulted in employment losses in certain areas. Since 1980, there exists a discernible increase in salary disparity in the United States as a result of the job polarization phenomena. With rapid advancements in automation, artificial intelligence, and digitalization, traditional job roles are being redefined, replaced, or augmented by technological innovations. The paper highlights the various dimensions of this technological disruption, including the displacement of workers, job polarization and wage inequalities. It explores the potential benefits and challenges that arise from this transformative process, such as increased productivity, and income inequality, and the importance of proactive policies to navigate this evolving landscape. This study offers insightful information about the intricate connection involving technology and employment by examining current trends and consulting pertinent research studies. It also gives readers a thorough grasp of the potential and difficulties that the digital era will present.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning, SVM, Random Forest, and XGBoost for Email Spam Detection: A Socio- Network Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: The surge in email usage has led to an upsurge in spam emails, posing threats to both security and user experience. In this era marked by ever-evolving cyber threats, the task of effectively detecting email spam remains critical. This research presents a comprehensive comparative analysis offour well-known machine learning techniques: Deep Learning, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and XGBoost, specifically aimed at detecting email spam. The approach goes beyond analyzing email content alone; it also considers the social network characteristics of emails to enhance overall detection accuracy. This involves examining factors such as sender-receiver relationships, temporal patterns, and the community structure within email networks. To ensure the robustness and real-world relevance of our analysis, the research employs a diverse and extensive dataset containing both legitimate and spam emails for training and evaluation. By bridging the gap between cutting-edge machine learning and email security, this study contributes to the ongoing efforts to combat the growing menace of email spam.

articleTitle: A Study of Transliteration Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computing, Communication, and Intelligent Systems (ICCCIS)
abstract: In the present era, text generated by users is becoming increasingly popular on the Internet. People rely on search engines for their information. The transliterated text is one of the major concerns to search the relevant information for a user query. There is a corresponding effort to handle transliterated text in order to take advantage of this huge knowledge source. In this paper we review the most recent findings in the domain of transliteration. Firstly, start with an introduction to transliteration and its challenges, then outline several transliteration methods and discuss new research efforts in information search for transliterated text. In this study, the authors present various approaches/techniques, algorithms, and evaluation approaches of previous studies, identify some important issues in machine transliteration approaches/models, and provide future guidance for researchers in this field.
